title: feat(post): pattern folders with linear and grid copies at the post
body:
Effort: high

## What changed

This PR adds a pattern folder to the operation list. A folder holds member operations of one setup. The post writes the members again at each enabled copy of a linear or grid pattern. All copies use the WCS of the setup: the moves shift, and the work offset stays the same.

- Schema: `PatternDef` in `crates/app/src/schema.rs`. It has `setup`, `suppressed`, `order_mode` (`ByTool` is the default, or `ByPart`), `kind` (`Linear` or `Grid`), `members` and `disabled_instances`. The copy numbers start at 1. Copy 1 is where the members are now.
- Row law: a folder is a list row, the same as a Pause entry. It uses `OperationMeta::order` for its position. Its members stand directly after it, in folder order. The commands keep this order. A member moves only inside its folder.
- Commands (`crates/app/src/commands/pattern_folder.rs`): `CreatePatternFolder`, `EditPatternFolder`, `SetPatternMembers`, `SetPatternInstanceEnabled` and `DeletePatternFolder`. Delete ungroups the members. Each command is undoable.
  - `ReorderOperation` and `RenameOperation` take folders.
  - `DeleteOperation` and `DeleteEntity` remove a deleted member from its folder. Undo puts it back.
- Validation at command creation: the command checks counts (1-1000), the total copies (10000 at most), spacings (finite, above 0) and directions (finite, in XY, not zero). Grid directions must not be parallel. It also checks members: each is a milling operation, is not a probe, is in one setup, is named once and is in no other folder. Nested folders are not possible because a member must be an operation. At least one copy must stay on.
- cl: `cl::transform::copies` (`crates/cl/src/cl/transform_copies.rs`) joins the translated copies of one path. Between two copies, the link goes straight up to the clearance plane, across, then straight down. Cycle anchors and compensated spans move with their copy. Plasma and tilted moves are refused by name.
- Posting (`crates/app/src/posting_pattern.rs`):
  - `ByTool`: each member is one section over all enabled copies, so it has one `T.. M6`.
  - `ByPart`: all members cut one copy, then the next copy. The after-action and the setup-change stop go only on the last section of each operation.
  - The post refuses these cases by name: a turned or flipped WCS, a member that is missing or in another setup, and members that are not directly after the folder.
  - `viewer_map` maps every line of every copy.
  - Per-operation files refuse a `ByPart` folder by name.
- Verification gate: each shifted copy is checked against the machine travel of the setup (`MachineCheck::check_path`) and against its fixtures (`fixture_struck::op_hits`). A not-judged line names the folders whose other copies the stock sim does not judge.
- Project file: a new entity kind, `pattern`, with no version step. A document with no folder saves the same bytes as before. An older build refuses the unknown kind by name. The folder's display name is saved too.
- MCP (`crates/app/src/mcp/pattern_tools.rs`): new tools `create_pattern_folder`, `edit_pattern_folder`, `set_pattern_members`, `set_pattern_instance_enabled` and `delete_pattern_folder`. `get_job` lists `pattern_folders` only when the document has one. `rename_operation` and `reorder_operation` accept a folder.
- Docs: I regenerated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`, and I added a row to the guide table (`site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md`). The camcraft-mcp skill has new tool rows (process file).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3012-pattern-folder.md`.

Process change: yes (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`: the new MCP tool rows only).

## Review fix (head `07cd14690`)

This commit closes the findings of the review of `eaa90f1d6`.

- A pattern folder is not a model. `model::is_model` excludes it, thus `model_entities`, `get_job` and the laws that read them do not see a folder.
- The load checks the membership law over the whole file (`pattern_dto::validate_members`). It refuses a member that is not an operation row of the file. It refuses an operation that two folders name. The check runs before any world write.
- The post plan and the copy gate refuse by name an operation that two active folders name. A folder takes its members by name, not by a count of the rows that follow.
- The MCP tools refuse a `dir` entry that is not a number.

New pins, in `crates/app/tests/mcp/pattern_folder_law.rs` (`mcp` directory suite):

- `pattern_folder_law::a_folder_is_not_a_model`
- `pattern_folder_law::a_file_breaking_the_membership_law_is_refused_at_load`
- `pattern_folder_law::two_folders_that_name_one_operation_refuse_the_post_by_name`
- `pattern_folder_law::a_by_part_stop_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy`
- `pattern_folder_law::a_by_part_setup_change_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy`
- `pattern_folder_law::a_copy_that_strikes_a_fixture_blocks_the_post_until_it_is_off`
- `pattern_folder_law::a_copy_outside_the_machine_travel_blocks_the_post_until_it_is_off`

Mutation checks on this head (the guard removed, the 15 `pattern_folder*` tests run, the guard put back):

| Mutation | Red pins |
|---|---|
| `is_model` has no folder clause | `a_folder_is_not_a_model` |
| The load does not call `validate_members` | `a_file_breaking_the_membership_law_is_refused_at_load` |
| `refusal` does not check a second owner | `two_folders_that_name_one_operation_refuse_the_post_by_name` |
| The after-action goes on each by-part section (`posting.rs:1321`) | `a_by_part_stop_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy`, `a_by_part_setup_change_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy` |
| The setup change goes on each by-part section (`posting.rs:1361`) | `a_by_part_setup_change_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy` |
| `pattern_problems` judges no folder | the fixture pin, the travel pin, the two-folder pin |
| `dir` drops an entry that is not a number | `a_folder_is_not_a_model` (the `dir` assert) |
| `enabled_offsets` ignores `disabled_instances` | 5 pins, with the "copy 2 is not cut" assert of the by-tool pin |

With each guard put back, 15 of 15 tests pass.

One change has no pin of its own: the plan takes the members by name and not by count. The row-law refusal and the second-owner refusal together make the two forms give the same sections. Thus no test can see the difference.

Gate results on `07cd14690`, against `upstream/main` `4d891498e`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 1231 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (24.5 min). The `cl` change makes the quick tier fall back to the batch plan. The run includes `clippy -D warnings`, `app suites: mcp`, and `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 of 6 steps pass (9.3 min).

No golden changed in this commit.

## Tests

The results below are from the first head (`eaa90f1d6`). The section "Review fix" has the results of the final head.

These pins are in the `mcp` directory suite (`crates/app/tests/mcp/pattern_folder.rs`, `pattern_folder_post.rs`) and in the cl unit tests:

- `pattern_folder::a_folder_is_created_reordered_renamed_and_undone`
- `pattern_folder::edits_members_copies_and_delete_are_undoable`
- `pattern_folder::bad_patterns_and_members_are_refused_when_the_command_is_made`
- `pattern_folder::folders_round_trip_and_documents_without_them_write_no_key`
- `pattern_folder_post::by_tool_posts_each_member_once_over_every_enabled_copy`: linear, copy 2 off, golden. The tool changes are the same as the program without the folder.
- `pattern_folder_post::by_part_posts_every_member_at_one_copy_then_the_next`: grid, copy 4 off, golden, and the per-op refusal.
- `pattern_folder_post::a_folder_the_post_cannot_write_refuses_by_name`: out-of-block member order, turned WCS.
- `pattern_folder_post::mcp_tools_create_edit_reorder_undo_save_and_open_a_folder`
- `cl::transform::copies::tests::*` (6 tests)

Mutation checks (each guard file put back to `upstream/main`, then the pins run):

- `posting.rs`: the by-tool, by-part and refusal pins are red.
- `commands/operation/meta.rs`, `commands/delete_entity.rs` and `posting_per_op.rs`: the reorder, delete, rename, MCP and per-op pins are red.
- With the fix restored, all pins are green.

Gate results, against `upstream/main`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: the cl change makes the quick tier fall back to the batch tier, with 1231 steps (36.4 min).
  - 1230 steps passed. This includes every app suite and the `example_catalog*` suites.
  - The one failure was a clippy lint (`err().expect()`) in the new per-op pin. Commit `eaa90f1d6` fixes it.
  - On the final head `eaa90f1d6`, the gate's own `clippy -D warnings` step and the `app suites: mcp` step ran again. Both are green.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 of 6 steps pass (15.9 min).
- Heavy lanes: not run (see "Not exercised"). `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 116 steps.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

There are two new goldens, made with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`. No existing golden changed.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/pattern_folder/fanuc_linear_by_tool.nc`: 3 sections and 3 tool changes. Each link between copies is one `G00` at Z25.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/pattern_folder/fanuc_grid_by_part.nc`: 7 sections. Face1 is first, then Face2 and Face3 at copies 1, 2 and 3.

The example catalog suites ran as part of the gate. They have no folder, so their output does not change.

At the start of each copy, a `G00` repeats the point where the link ended. This line comes from the face path's own first rapid. It does not move the tool.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes: I did not run them. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) says that a P6 PR gets no heavy step. `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` shows the reach.
- The stock sim and the gouge check judge each member at copy 1 only. The stock-bounds check for the copies is also not done. This work is #3013. The not-judged line says this on every surface that reports the post.
- If a setup has no machine, the travel of a shifted copy is not checked. The program's own limit check still uses the default machine.
- The link rapid between two copies (by tool) is not part of the copy gate. `pattern_problems` judges each copy alone, against the machine travel and the fixtures. The link is at the clearance height or above, and the first-rapid law refuses a clearance height below a fixture top. #3013 lists the check of each link between copies.
- The review made two optional remarks that this PR does not change: the text of `TransformError::TiltedMove` says "mirrored" for a copy, and `posting.rs` is longer than 400 lines.
- UI: the browser shows a folder as a plain row. The folder UI is #3016.
- G52 and M98 output for compact programs is #3017.
- `verification_report` translates each copy of each member when it runs. A very large pattern can make the report slow.

## Overlaps

These PRs change the same files but other functions. The PR that merges second must refresh:

- #4288: `posting.rs` (`post_serves`, `HeightRefs`) and `project/file.rs` (`ToolKindDto`).
- #4368: `schema.rs`, `delete_entity.rs`, `mcp/mod.rs` and `mcp/tools.rs` (append rows).
- #4379 and #4173: `project/file.rs`.
- #4302 and #4238: `mcp/mod.rs` and `mcp/tools.rs`.
- #4383: `lib.rs`.
- #3103: `mcp/job.rs`.

Refs #3013 (in part: the travel and fixture checks for each copy).

Changelog: Pattern folders: post member operations again at each copy of a linear or grid pattern. Cut by tool (one tool change for each operation) or by part. Each copy can be turned off. There are undoable commands, MCP tools and project save.

Fixes #3012
